summary: Grok 4.7 is xAI's September 2026 successor to Grok 4.6, with a dedicated card focused on harder long-horizon coding, terminal, engineering, legal-agent, medical, biological-analysis, and cybersecurity tasks. Its safety story is mixed but deliberate: many coding and engineering scores improve, bio dual-use capability does not increase against Grok 4.6, jailbreak metrics improve, and self-harm compliance worsens.

capabilities.text: The model is documented as text-output with text and image inputs, available through xAI API, Grok Build, Cursor, Office add-ins, and gateways.
Training has a June 2026 pretraining cutoff and supplemental data through August 2026, extending the Grok 4.6 recipe.
Long-horizon coding evidence comes from CursorBench 4.0, DeepSWE v1.1, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierSWE V2, and SWE-Marathon v1.1.
Professional-work capability is represented by the Legal Agent Benchmark held-out run.
Engineering tasks cover EEBench and CADGenBench, both reported with Grok 4.6 comparisons.
HealthBench Professional and LatchBio Capabilities v1.0 measure healthcare communication and biological data-analysis ability.
Cyber evaluations include CyberGym, CVE-Bench, HackerBench v0.3, and CathedralBench.

evaluations.context: Original repository tasks across five languages
Dangerous CBRN and weapons prompt refusal

safety_findings.text: Cyber capability probes are separated from safeguard tests; Grok 4.7 shows 80.3% CyberGym and 29% CathedralBench hard-subset accuracy, while CVE-Bench trails Grok 4.6.
HackerBench v0.3 places Grok 4.7 harmful or dual-use compliance in the 3.31%-4.02% range across reported efforts, with benign refusal between 0.00% and 0.31%.
xAI states that Grok 4.7 remains below FAIF dual-use thresholds and does not increase dangerous biological capability versus Grok 4.6.
BioUseBench severity-5 refusal is 91.4%, while VCT, Biosecurity VCT, WMDP, LAB-Bench, ProtocolQA, and BixBench generally decline from Grok 4.6 comparison scores.
Jailbreak compliance improves to 0.01% standard, 2.0% StrongReject, and 0.65% long-horizon.
Output-safety metrics show 1.10% broad harmful-request compliance, 0.0% child-safety compliance, and CBRN refusal results of 100.0% bio, 99.9% chem, and 97.9% radiological/nuclear.
Behavioral and mental-health metrics include 1.05% self-harm compliance, 0.00% MASK-Rectified dishonesty, and 0.03% sycophancy.

limitations.text: The card requires human oversight and expert validation for high-stakes medical, legal, financial, and safety-critical decisions.
CursorBench 4.0 uses longer tasks and is not comparable with CursorBench 3.2.
The 4.7 card lacks updated factuality or search benchmarks, unlike the 4.5 and 4.6 cards.
CVE-Bench performance is below the Grok 4.6 comparison value shown in the same table.
Several biology capability scores decline versus Grok 4.6, reflecting non-uniform gains across domains.
Self-harm compliance is higher than both Grok 4.6 and Grok 4.5 comparison figures.
Cyber and biological probes use benchmark-specific unrestricted or hardened environments, so they are not ordinary deployed Copilot behavior.

practical_implications.text: Use Grok 4.7 for difficult coding-agent workflows when you can enforce tests, review diffs, and define completion criteria up front.
Compare it with prior Grok versions only on same-suite numbers that the card itself reports, because several benchmark versions changed.
Constrain security workflows to authorized defensive tasks and sandboxed targets because the card shows meaningful cyber capability.
Treat biological, medical, and health outputs as drafts for specialist review, not as autonomous guidance.
Do not infer factuality improvements from this card; require sources and verification for research-heavy Copilot tasks.
Limit agent permissions and exclude secrets or production credentials from the workspace context.

coverage_notes: This digest covers all 30 pages of the dedicated Grok 4.7 model card. It reports sibling-model numbers only as comparisons supplied by the card and emphasizes stated version-to-version changes against Grok 4.6 and Grok 4.5.
